- The changes alter verdicts, so they are not optional extras. Four examples follow.
  - Design: three or more of eight molecules outside the band of normal diffusion refutes the one-nanosecond claim. Gate: this only adds a label (item D3a).
  - Design: the proxy must beat inverse diffusion and simulated density by the spread between reruns. Gate: judge only against the three orderings that need no simulation (item D3d).
  - Design: disagreement between fit windows leaves the main claim "not established". Gate: it is only downgraded to "window-dependent" (item D3b).
  - Design: a rank correlation below 0.8 refutes the main claim. Gate: it refutes only the one proxy formula tested (item D1).
- The gate also queued nine controls that the design lacks.
  - One is an early speed check that stops a run that is too slow (item D5).
  - By the gate's arithmetic, a box three times slower than guessed spends about $13.2 without it. With it, about $3.3.
  - Two more: a hand-computed density for every built box (item I2), and a planted check of the proxy formula (item I3).
  - Four more are planted checks: the family count (I7), the noise margin (I8), the other fit windows (I10), and joined trajectories (I5).
  - The last two: a long-lag slope readout (F2), and a check that time comes from step number times timestep (I12).
- In all, twelve gate answers change the build: three rejections (D1, D3, F1) and nine queued controls.
- Building the design alone ships verdict rules the gate rejected. It also drops a control that caps spend.
- Building the gate's version departs from the build instruction. Choosing between them is not the builder's call.

BLOCKER 2. The design builds the simulation boxes on this workstation, and this workstation cannot.
- The design says boxes are "built and checked on the local workstation" before launch, at no rented-box cost.
- The checks are a builder review, a charge check per molecule, and a zero-step read.
- A zero-step read loads each box into the simulation program without moving any atoms.
- The gate's density check (item I2) also relies on that read. It stops the run before launch on a mismatch.
- On 2026-10-18, none of the three programs this needs was installed here.
  - The chemistry toolkit (RDKit) is missing: "No module named 'rdkit'".
  - The box-packing program (Packmol) is not on the path. There is no Fortran compiler to build it.
  - The simulation program (LAMMPS) has no executable and no Python module here.
- No conda installation exists either. The system Python is 3.14.4.
- The build instruction also has the on-box script run every stage in order.
- That would build the boxes on the rented box, which the design rules out.
- So the pre-launch step is not runnable as given. Installing a toolchain, or moving the step to the box, would be a patch.

ALSO TO SETTLE, in the same directive or in the launcher copy. The operating notes already allow launcher edits to folder, payload and forwarded settings.
- The frozen bootstrap (/home/hal/dev/interp/dm_hack/latent_skeptic_meta/experiments/coolant_proxy/frozen/remote_run.sh) checks for a language-model stack.
- It requires a card-enabled torch and a Gemma-2 model class. Neither has any use in this run.
- It has no recipe for a simulation program with graphics-card (GPU) support. The design's one-hour setup for that is marked GUESS.
- That bootstrap enters ~/mats_manifold. The frozen launcher copies code to ~/welfare_probe. The two frozen files disagree as shipped.
- The design's clock rule divides 18.0 by the hourly price. The launcher forwards no price setting.
- The launcher's default remote time cap is 5400 seconds. The plan is 12.54 hours.
- The launcher fetches the box's out/ folder. The build instruction puts results in results_cp1/out/.
- The design never sets the packing density for the builder. The builder's default is 0.75 g/cm³. Its README example uses 0.3 g/cm³.

3. Name the setting the launcher copy will forward for the hourly price. Name the packing density to use.
